what_it_does: High-speed electrical connections in data centers and network switches (like the cables linking servers together) degrade signal quality through reflection, crosstalk from neighboring signals, and power loss. This paper presents a tiny integrated chip that measures these distortions in real time across frequencies up to 40 GHz (billions of cycles per second). The chip uses a measurement technique called time-domain reflectometry—sending pulses down the connection and watching how they bounce back—to diagnose signal problems. The innovation is fitting this measurement capability into a compact, power-efficient form, using just 99.5 milliwatts per port, making it practical to embed in high-density switch hardware.
